sourceEnglishTitle: Explain the Roof System to a New Hire
sourceEnglishObjective: Walk a new hire through every layer of the roof, in order, and say why each one is there
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI is a new hire on day one: walk them from the deck to the ridge, name each layer in order, and explain why each one goes where it does using primero, luego, porque and por eso.
sourceSpanishReaderTitle: From the Deck to the Ridge

sourceGrammarExamples.es: Empezamos abajo porque el agua corre hacia abajo.
sourceGrammarExamples.en: We start at the bottom because water runs downhill.

sourceGrammarExamples.es: El agua corre hacia abajo; por eso empezamos abajo.
sourceGrammarExamples.en: Water runs downhill; that's why we start at the bottom.

example.target: Rogelio le explica el sistema de techo antes de subir.
example.native: Rogelio explains the roof system to him before they go up.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Preterite: expliqué (c changes to qu), explicó.

example.native: That's why we start from the bottom.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Stem change e to ie, except in the nosotros form: empezamos.

example.target: El agua siempre corre hacia abajo.
Cada hilera cubre la de abajo.
example.native: Each course covers the one below.

example.target: En el alero ponemos el goterón.
example.native: At the eave we put the drip edge.

candidateObjective: 新人に屋根の各層を順に示し、それぞれの役割を説明する。
candidateFocus: まず、次に、最後に order the layers. ～ので and そのために connect a layer's position with its purpose; customer-facing questions use a more polite register.

archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Rogelio explains the roof system to him before they go up.

archivedSpeaking.opening: まず野地板、次に下葺き材と防水膜、最後に棟換気材と棟包み材です。各層の役割を順に説明します。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Lead a new hire through the roof layers from deck to ridge. Name each layer in order and explain its role with natural Japanese sequencing such as まず and 次に.

reader.sourceSpanish: Hoy es el primer día de Kevin en la cuadrilla, y Rogelio le explica el sistema de techo antes de subir.
reader.sourceEnglish: Today is Kevin's first day on the crew, and Rogelio explains the roof system to him before they go up.
reader.candidateJapanese: 今日はケビンが作業班に入った初日で、ロヘリオが屋根に上がる前に屋根の構成を説明します。
reader.archivedJapanese: 今日はケビンが作業班に入った初日で、ロヘリオが屋根に上がる前に屋根の構成を説明します。
reader.archivedEnglish: Today is Kevin's first day on the crew, and Rogelio explains the roof system to him before they go up.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Cada capa tiene su trabajo, y todas trabajan juntas.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Each layer has its job, and they all work together.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「各層にはそれぞれ役割があり、すべてが一緒に働きます。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「各層にはそれぞれ役割があり、すべてが一緒に働きます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Each layer has its job, and they all work together.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Primero va la cubierta y luego la sub-capa.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: First comes the deck, then the underlayment.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「まず野地板を敷き、次に下葺き材を敷きます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: First comes the deck, then the underlayment.
reader.reviewNote: Layer order depends on roof-system details; the source teaches a scene, not a universal installation sequence.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: La cubierta es la base, así que tiene que estar firme y seca.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: The deck is the base, so it has to be solid and dry.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「野地板は土台なので、しっかりしていて乾いている必要があります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: The deck is the base, so it has to be solid and dry.
reader.reviewNote: Solid/dry deck conditions need product and site-specific confirmation before scored instruction.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: En el alero ponemos el goterón, porque el agua tiene que caer en la canaleta y no en la madera.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: At the eave we put the drip edge, because the water has to fall into the gutter and not onto the wood.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「軒先には水切り板金を取り付けます。水を木部ではなく雨どいに落とすためです。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: At the eave we put the drip edge, because the water has to fall into the gutter and not onto the wood.
reader.reviewNote: Drip edge placement and gutter drainage depend on design and manufacturer; trade review required.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: En el alero y en la limahoya también va la membrana impermeable, porque ahí corre más agua.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: At the eave and in the valley the ice and water shield goes on too, because more water runs there.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「軒先と谷部にはアイス・アンド・ウォーター・シールドも敷きます。そこにはより多くの水が流れるからです。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: At the eave and in the valley the ice and water shield goes on too, because more water runs there.
reader.reviewNote: Ice-and-water shield at eave/valley depends on climate, product and code; do not teach as universal.

reader.sourceSpanish: Kevin: ¿Y por qué no empezamos arriba, donde está la cumbrera?
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin: And why don't we start at the top, where the ridge is?
reader.candidateJapanese: ケビン「なぜ棟のある上から始めないのですか。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ケビン「なぜ棟のある上から始めないのですか。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Kevin: And why don't we start at the top, where the ridge is?

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Porque el agua siempre corre hacia abajo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Because water always runs downhill.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「水は常に低い方へ流れるからです。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「水は常に低い方へ流れるからです。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Because water always runs downhill.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Por eso empezamos desde abajo: primero la hilera inicial y después las tejas asfálticas, una hilera encima de otra.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That's why we start from the bottom: first the starter strip and then the asphalt shingles, one course on top of another.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「そのため下から始めます。まずスターター材、次にアスファルトシングル材を一段ずつ重ねます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That's why we start from the bottom: first the starter strip and then the asphalt shingles, one course on top of another.
reader.reviewNote: Starter/shingle sequence and overlap are system-specific; trade review required.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Cada hilera cubre la de abajo, así que el agua pasa por encima y nunca por debajo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Each course covers the one below, so the water runs over it and never under it.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「各段が下の段を覆うので、水はその上を流れ、下には入りません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Each course covers the one below, so the water runs over it and never under it.
reader.reviewNote: Never under it is too absolute for actual roof performance; retain source wording as evidence and qualify before scoring.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Alrededor de la chimenea y de las paredes ponemos el tapajuntas, porque esas uniones son los puntos débiles.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Around the chimney and the walls we put flashing, because those joints are the weak points.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「煙突や壁の周りには水切り板金を取り付けます。その接合部は弱い箇所だからです。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Around the chimney and the walls we put flashing, because those joints are the weak points.
reader.reviewNote: Flashing details at chimney/wall are design-specific; trade review required.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Al final, arriba de todo, va la ventilación de caballete y luego el caballete.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: At the end, at the very top, goes the ridge vent and then the ridge cap.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「最後に一番上へ棟換気材を取り付け、その上に棟包み材を取り付けます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: At the end, at the very top, goes the ridge vent and then the ridge cap.
reader.reviewNote: Ridge vent/cap sequence is system-specific; trade review required.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: El ático necesita respirar; por eso dejamos la ventilación en la cumbrera.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: The attic needs to breathe; that's why we leave the vent at the ridge.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「屋根裏には換気が必要なので、棟に換気材を設けます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: The attic needs to breathe; that's why we leave the vent at the ridge.
reader.reviewNote: Ridge ventilation design is not universal; trade review required.

reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「説明は伝わっていますか。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「説明は伝わっていますか。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Kevin: Sí, primero la base, luego la protección contra el agua y al final la ventilación.
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin: Yes, first the base, then the protection against water, and at the end the ventilation.
reader.candidateJapanese: ケビン「はい。まず土台、次に水からの保護、最後に換気ですね。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ケビン「はい。まず土台、次に水からの保護、最後に換気ですね。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Kevin: Yes, first the base, then the protection against water, and at the end the ventilation.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Exacto, y si tienes dudas, pregúntame lo que quieras.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Exactly, and if you have questions, ask me anything you want.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「その通りです。疑問があれば何でも質問してください。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「その通りです。疑問があれば何でも質問してください。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Exactly, and if you have questions, ask me anything you want.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Con un cliente se dice así: Si tiene dudas, pregúnteme a mí.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: With a client you say it this way: If you have questions, ask me.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「お客様には『ご質問があれば、私にお尋ねください』と言います。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「お客様には『ご質問があれば、私にお尋ねください』と言います。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: With a client you say it this way: If you have questions, ask me.
